newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan says Ethiopia killed many state officials.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says Ethiopia killed many state officials.

text.p: Sudan said on Monday that Ethiopia had killed the governor of Kurmuk, one of the first towns to fall in fighting between the army and rebels.

"The attacking Tigrayan (Ethiopian) troops killed Yacoub Hussien, the governor of Kurmuk and Qamareddin Ismail, the secretary general of a state Islamic organisation," Information Minister Al-Tayeb Ibrahim Mohamad Khair told a news briefing.
A Sudanese government daily had said earlier that the rebels had taken hostage several government officials at Kurmuk and that two of them had died.

It did not say how or when they were killed and named them as Rabei Ahmed Kurmino, chairman of the town council, and Ismail Mahmoud, local head of the National Congress, the only political system in Sudan.

Sudan says Ethiopia and Eritrea are fighting with rebels who want to take a strategic dam near the southeastern town of Damazin to put pressure on Khartoum's Islamist government and spark a popular uprising.
Both African states deny any reports of foreign interference and the rebels say that they singlehandedly started the offensive earlier this month.
The rebels have said that Iran has given the Sudanese army weapons, including banned chemical arms, cash and even troops to help with the fighting.
Tayeb denied the rebel reports of Iranian assistance but told the briefing that Sudan had the right to ask for help as it was facing a foreign invasion.
"If we are facing the rebel Sudan Peoples Liberation Army that would not be a problem as they are finished. What we are facing is an aggression from outside and we can ask for assistance," he said.
